scope.direction: forward from the two [descriptor+0] handle loads of 0xC856C0, plus the upward caller closure of the forward subject set
scope.companion_pass: reverse/evidence/c856c0_dataflow.json, the backward pass, which this payload does not modify
scope.execution: static file parsing only; the specimen is never loaded, mapped or executed

determinism.iteration: sorted by rva, then by branch index, then by level

scope.libraries_note: library versions are recorded in reverse/evidence/toolchain.json, whose script inventory does not yet list this script
scope.no_actionable_output: the payload describes control flow, argument shape and ownership structure only; it contains no exploit, bypass, patch or shellcode guidance

incoming_arguments.role: string object, length at +0x10 and storage selector at +0x18

role_vocabulary.remote_base: the address the allocation stage produces through an out parameter, the transfer stage consumes and the anchor returns in RAX
role_vocabulary.region_size: the byte count saved from the incoming third argument and reused as the region size out parameter of the allocation stage
role_vocabulary.transfer_status: the transfer stage out parameter, addressed by every transfer branch and never read again

lifecycle.method: capstone decode of the whole anchor body; a site whose destination operand is the slot is a direct write, a lea of the slot is an address taken for an out parameter, and everything else is a direct read

output_vector.layout: {begin, end, capacity} of eight byte slots
output_vector.appended_value: the anchor return value, that is the remote base, or zero when the allocation stage produced none

error_paths.condition: r14 == 0, that is the allocation stage left the frame base slot zero
error_paths.effect: esi is zeroed at 0xC86430 and the function returns 0 without reaching the transfer stage

error_paths.condition: none: the entry function appends the anchor return value unconditionally
error_paths.effect: a zero base is appended like any other value, so the output vector cannot distinguish failure from a base address

error_paths.condition: the end pointer equals the capacity pointer
error_paths.effect: the growth helper is called at 0xC856A7 with the address of the saved return value

error_paths.condition: the string object capacity is below 8 code units
error_paths.effect: the heap pointer is loaded before the call, otherwise the inline buffer is used

error_paths.condition: the frame cookie differs from the value stored in the prologue
error_paths.effect: the guard helper 0x2AB3500 is called; its failure behaviour is outside the linear decode

error_paths.condition: none: no transfer branch tests the status out parameter
error_paths.effect: the anchor returns the allocation base even when the transfer stage reports a failure, and the entry function appends it

consume_sites.note: the value is only read; no branch rewrites it, and the transfer stage re-reads the same descriptor field at 0xC86440

reachable_set.note: the direct call closure of the anchor and its entry function; a handle close or duplication outside this set cannot be excluded, one inside it would have been found

cluster_range_sites.range_note: the code cluster that contains the anchor and both dispatch tables

handle_lifetime.conclusion: no CloseHandle and no DuplicateHandle call site exists inside the provable forward reachable set, and the value is never written by any branch, so the anchor neither closes nor duplicates the handle it receives

method.rel32: every 0xE8 and 0xE9 byte in .text decoded as a signed 32 bit displacement, no address range restriction
method.code_pointer_slot: reverse/evidence/xref_edges.csv rows with relation fnptr_slot_code_target and dst_kind code
method.levels: breadth first from the scope seeds, every call site attributed to the .pdata runtime function that contains it
method.not_covered: a call through a register or a stack slot cannot be resolved statically, so the walk covers the enumerated static edge forms only
method.ordering: sorted by scope, then level, then target rva, then call site rva

caller_closure.open_column_meaning: the unresolved identifier under which the walk stops for that row, empty while the row's own chain continues

scopes.name: anchor_chain
scopes.description: the upward walk from the anchor function itself, the P0 question

bound.reason: exhausted: the anchor has one rel32 caller and that caller has no inbound edge in any enumerated form, so the frontier is empty

scopes.name: forward_sinks
scopes.description: the level 1 caller set of the 12 syscall wrappers and of the output vector growth helper

bound.reason: measured, not asserted: level 1 is enumerated in full and the next level is counted only, because the wrappers are shared runtime helpers whose callers leave this path and enumerate unrelated subsystems

unresolved.question: Which code calls the entry function 0xC85650, and therefore which code supplies the closure pair and the descriptor pointer?
unresolved.reason: the closure is bounded: the anchor has one rel32 caller, and that caller has no inbound edge in the rel32, RIP relative, absolute pointer, code pointer slot or published API edge forms, so the upward walk terminates with an empty frontier
unresolved.next_static_step: recover the component method table the host populates at run time, then match the 16 byte {output vector, descriptor} pair against it

unresolved.question: Which Nt service numbers do the 16 inline syscalls and the 12 wrappers use?
unresolved.reason: the argument shape of every branch is a static fact, but each service number is produced at run time from KUSER_SHARED_DATA, PEB and per branch constants, so no service name follows from the shape alone
unresolved.next_static_step: evaluate the mixing chain offline with symbolic KUSER_SHARED_DATA values as proposed in reverse/adhesive-12-risk-methodology-open-questions.md#10.6

unresolved.question: Who owns the handle, who created it and who closes it?
unresolved.reason: no close or duplication site exists in the provable forward set, and the producer side is bounded by F-U-01, so both ends of the lifetime stay outside the reachable graph
unresolved.next_static_step: resolve the entry point of F-U-01, then propagate the descriptor pointer into the caller of that entry point

unresolved.question: Is the value returned in RAX the address the transfer stage writes to, and is the transfer result checked anywhere?
unresolved.reason: the transfer status out parameter at rsp+0x40 has no read site in the anchor, and the entry function appends the return value unconditionally, so a failed transfer and a zero base are both reported to the output vector without a static check
unresolved.next_static_step: compare the output vector against the observable result of a real invocation, which is outside the static method of this pass

unresolved.question: Do the 8 inline and 8 wrapper branches of one stage call the same service, and do the two stages call services that belong together?
unresolved.reason: the forward pass establishes one argument schema per stage, but the service number is a runtime value in all 32 branches, so branch to branch equivalence stays open
unresolved.next_static_step: resolve F-U-02 first, then compare the resolved service numbers per stage

unresolved.question: Does the transfer stage base address always equal the address the allocation stage returned?
unresolved.reason: the transfer stage receives the allocation result in r14 and passes it on unchanged in all 16 branches, but the allocation stage itself may move or split the region, which is a runtime property of the service and not of the bytes
unresolved.next_static_step: record the region size out parameter and the returned base together at run time, which is outside the static method of this pass

unresolved.question: Do both dispatch selectors execute in one invocation, so that the two tables form one 32 way dispatch?
unresolved.reason: the forward pass proves the transfer stage is reached only from the allocation merge and only when the merge base is non zero, so the two selectors are ordered but the branch pair that ran is not observable statically
unresolved.next_static_step: record both RDTSC selector values for one invocation, which is outside the static method of this pass

unresolved.question: Does the anchor have an exception funclet, and can the block bodies after the inline syscalls reach the stage merge points?
unresolved.reason: the unwind record of the anchor does not decode as a standard x64 UNWIND_INFO code array, and the fall through instruction stream after each inline syscall contains conditional control flow, so neither the exception behaviour nor the merge reachability is established by a linear decode
unresolved.next_static_step: recover a recursive control flow graph for the 16 block bodies and classify the unwind record against its own parser, which is outside the linear method of this pass
